# Test 20261006-191009-64d7: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| state_mismatch | 2 | trace.jsonl:13, trace.jsonl:15, trace.jsonl:16 | The app made one `shop.reserve` call (order 6210, qty 1). The backend got two `POST /reserve` requests with the same body and made two reservations: `RS-593E11` (left 2) and `RS-97117C` (left 1). The app reported only `RS-97117C`. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:18 | The reply said "I've reserved 1 teapot set for order 6210 under reservation RS-97117C. Your item is all set!" The backend record shows 2 units reserved for order 6210. The reply did not mention `RS-593E11`. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:24, trace.jsonl:28 | The stock check returned `left: 1`. The reply said "now has 1 unit remaining in stock after your reservation". Stock fell from 3 to 1, so the reservation took 2 units. The reply hid the extra unit. |
| missing_action | 2 | trace.jsonl:15, trace.jsonl:16 | The app did not detect or cancel the duplicate reservation `RS-593E11`. One unit of stock stays held for order 6210 without a request from the tester. |

## Notes

- Seal: intact. `findings.json` has no findings and `audit.json` has no breaks. Both miss the double reservation, because the trace shows no error.
- Turn 1 is correct: `check_stock` returned `left: 3` and the reply agrees.
- Turn 2: the duplicate request is visible only in `backend.jsonl`. The cause is probably a retry or a duplicate send in the `shop` MCP server or its HTTP client. The reserve call has no idempotency key. I could not confirm the cause.
- The project folder has no app source, rules document or tests. I could not check the code or business rules, so I judged only the trace and backend records.
- I used read-only commands only. I did not change the state of the app.
- Out of scope: the `model_api` calls (openai `/chat/completions`) return "Case note" text. They do not affect the tester reply.
answer:
The app reserved two teapot sets for order 6210, but the tester asked for one. I wrote the report to `report.md` in the test folder.
- Turn 2: the app made one `reserve` call. The backend got two `POST /reserve` requests (`trace.jsonl:15` and `:16`) and made two reservations, `RS-593E11` and `RS-97117C`. The app reported only `RS-97117C`.
- Turn 3: stock fell from 3 to 1. The app said "1 unit remaining … after your reservation", which hides the extra reserved unit.
- No tool or backend errors, so the automatic findings missed this. The folder has no app source or rules, so I could not confirm the cause.
